subject: Debugging button hint for shiny development

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: Debugging button hint for shiny development
parts:
I've been off-list for a while, so this sort of thing may be common knowledge, but here's a simple trick discovered by a bay area programmer to make debugging easier:


 => Browse[1]>


When you are debugging or authoring a shiny application in RStudio or the console, debugging often means you have to add 'browser()' somewhere to the code and restart your application - which may lose state.

Here's how to add a button that drops back to the R console (or RStudio console) in the context of the server.

You can then run most code from your reactives (not any UI stuff) to find out why it's breaking.

When you are done, type c<enter> to resume your shiny app.

It keeps any objects you create from one click (and session) to the next.

In server.r:

  observe(label="console",{
    if(input$console != 0) {
      options(browserNLdisabled=TRUE)
      saved_console<-".RDuetConsole"
      if (file.exists(saved_console)) load(saved_console)
      isolate(browser())
      save(file=saved_console,list=ls(environment()))
    }
  })

In ui.r (in the sidebar or top bar perhaps):

        actionButton("console","server console"),

-Alex
